A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OCB framework and COCOLogic benchmark. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, aggregation and object-count ablations, and qualitative concept analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, feature-removal and sensitivity experiments, and detection-failure examples.

M1.justification: The proposal filtering, image/object concept extraction, five aggregation options and linear predictor remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. The shared-vocabulary and sparsity discussion clarifies the existing framework; nonsparse and object-only evaluations vary its configuration without introducing a new proposed component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PASCAL-VOC, COCO(h), COCO(l), SUN397 and COCOLogic with the same task coverage. COCOLogic's class rules and sample counts are unchanged. The added analyses vary configurations within these retained datasets.

E2.justification: v3 adds CLIP+MLP across all five benchmark settings in Table 1 and Coarse-to-Fine CBM (C2F-CBM) on SUN397 and COCOLogic in Table 2. These substantially broaden v1's comparisons with standard and equal-capacity SpLiCE-based CBMs.

E3.justification: Section 5 revises the stated COCOLogic metric from accuracy to balanced accuracy; retained numerical scores do not establish recomputation. Added protocols use a common LAION-based vocabulary and nonsparse OCB for the C2F-CBM comparison, and vary feature inputs, sparsity and minimum proposal size from 0.005 to 0.05.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained proposal-model, aggregation and object-count analyses, v3 adds image-only versus object-only controls (Table 4), capacity sweeps (Figure 8), minimum-size sensitivity (Table 10), and duplicate/irrelevant detection examples (Figure 9). These test additional explanations for gains and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations over five seeds. The new tables continue this practice, and the added checklist reiterates it. No increased run count, new uncertainty estimator or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 rows and v1 Tables 3–7, retained as v3 Tables 5–9, keep their numerical values. Substantial new results include C2F-CBM versus nonsparse OCB on SUN397 at 70.12 versus 89.60, object-only VOC performance of 77.48, CLIP+MLP scores, and capacity/size sweeps. These are added comparisons and configurations, not improvements to the earlier reported scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, filtering equations, aggregation formulas and COCOLogic rules are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs. The added qualitative sparsity explanation and discussion of linear-classifier limitations introduce no formal assumption, derivation or theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and four stated contributions retain their substantive claims. A limited novelty qualification occurs when v3 removes the introduction's 'first' qualifier for OCB, alongside acknowledging related object-based concept-bank work. The principal performance, multilabel-classification and benchmark contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the VOC ablation as evidence that global and object features are complementary, explicitly discusses linear-readout limitations on COCOLogic, and explains additional capacity, size and detection failures. These refine the existing account of applicability and noise sensitivity while retaining the original aggregation and pretrained-model limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code/data repository address in footnote 1 and states that COCOLogic scripts are provided there; v1 mentioned a repository without an address. The core Appendix C hyperparameters and hardware information remain unchanged. Repository contents or availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Prasse et al. (2025), DCBM, and distinguishes its image-level activation vector from OCB's combined image/object activations. The broader related-work coverage remains stable. Panousis et al.'s C2F-CBM was already cited in v1; its actual evaluation is new.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose are retained. v3 locally rewrites the introduction, evaluation discussion and conclusion, renames Section 5.4, subdivides Appendix E, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. This is limited restructuring rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 expands Table 1, adds comparison/ablation Tables 2, 4 and 10, and introduces the capacity plot and failure illustrations in Figures 8 and 9. It also revises Figures 4–5 captions and rearranges existing figures and appendix tables, substantially expanding the visual presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited comparator breadth and incomplete attribution of performance gains. The C2F-CBM and CLIP+MLP comparisons, broader capacity controls and global-feature ablation provide stronger tests of the central object-centric contribution, while failure examples clarify its limits. Reporting weaknesses remain: the metric revision leaves unchanged COCOLogic scores unexplained, and Table 10's COCOLogic trend is not consistently monotonic despite the accompanying prose. These weaknesses do not outweigh the substantially stronger comparative and diagnostic evidence.
